chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, who narrated that the hadith was raised to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Hanān ibn Sadīr Al-Sayrafi visited Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) while a group of his companions were with him. He said: 'O Hanān ibn Sadīr, do you visit Abā 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) once every month?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'What about once every two months?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'What about once a year?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you are toward your master!' He said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, it is due to lack of provisions and the long distance.' He said: 'Shall I not guide you to an accepted visitation even if the one visited is far?' He said: 'How should I visit him, O son of the Messenger of Allah?'

He said: 'Perform Ghusl on Friday or any day you wish, wear your purest clothes, ascend to the highest place in your house or the desert, and face the Qiblah with your face after it becomes clear that the grave is there.'
Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah.'

Then say: 'Peace be upon you, O my master and son of my master, and my leader and son of my leader. Peace be upon you, O my master, the Martyr and son of the Martyr, the Slain and son of the Slain. Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. I am visiting you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, with my heart, my tongue, and my limbs, even if I do not visit you physically to see your dome.'

Peace be upon you, O heir of Adam, the chosen one of Allah, and heir of Noah, the prophet of Allah, and heir of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah, and heir of Musa, the one spoken to by Allah, and heir of 'Isa, the spirit of Allah, and heir of Muhammad, the beloved of Allah, his prophet and messenger, and heir of 'Ali, Commander of the Faithful, the successor of the Messenger of Allah and his caliph, and heir of Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, the successor of the Commander of the Faithful.
May Allah curse those who killed you, and may He renew their punishment in this hour and in every hour.

I, O my master, seek nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Great, and to your grandfather, the Messenger of Allah, and to your father, the Commander of the Faithful, and to your brother, Al-Hasan, and to you, O my master. So peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah, by my visitation to you with my heart, my tongue, and all my limbs.

So be my intercessor for me, O my master, for the acceptance of that from me. And I seek nearness to Allah and to all of you by dissociating myself from your enemies and cursing them. So upon you be the prayers, pleasure, and mercy of Allah.
Then turn slightly to your left and turn your face toward the grave of 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn, who is at the feet of his father, and send peace upon him in the same manner.

Then supplicate to Allah for whatever you wish of the affairs of your religion and your world. Then pray four Rak'ahs, for the prayer of visitation can be eight, or six, or four, or two Rak'ahs, and the best is eight.

Then face toward the grave of Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and say: 'I bid farewell to you, O my master and son of my master, and O my leader and son of my leader. And I bid farewell to you, O my master and son of my master, O 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn. And I bid farewell to you, O my masters, O company of Martyrs.'
So upon you be the peace, mercy, pleasure, and blessings of Allah.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (ritual visit to the shrine of an Imam or Prophet)

ai.seo_question: How to perform Ziyarat for Imam Al-Husayn when living far away?
ai.summary: Compiled by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the theological validity of virtual visitation (*ziyat al-gha'ib*) by detailing a ritual that mirrors physical presence, including facing the Qibla and the grave, performing prayers, and reciting specific salutations. It emphasizes that spiritual proximity and sincerity (*qurb*) compensate for geographical distance, a concept rooted in the Quranic verse 'Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God' (2:115), which Hanan ibn Sadeer cites to justify the direction of prayer for distant pilgrims.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Barqi, from his father, who narrated that:

Ḥanān ibn Sadīr Al-Sayrafi went to (visit) Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) when a group of his companions were with him. Imam (a.s.) asked him, “O Ḥanān ibn Sadīr! Do you perform the Ziyārah of Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Ḥusain (a.s.)) once every month?” Ḥanān replied, “No.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “What about once every two months?” Ḥanān replied, “No.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “What about once a year?” Ḥanān replied, “No.” Imam (a.s.) said, “How negligent you people are toward your master!!!” Ḥanān said, “O son of the Messenger of Allāh! It is because of lack of wealth and the greatness of the distance.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Should I not teach you an accepted Ziyārah even from a great distance?!” Ḥanān asked, “How should I perform his Ziyārah, O son of the Messenger of Allāh?”

Imam (a.s.) replied: Perform a Ghusl on a Friday or any other day you wish, wear the most purified of your clothes, ascend to the highest place in your house or in a desert, and then face the Qiblah after ensuring that the grave is also in the same direction,
for Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, says, “Wherever you turn, there is the face of Allāh” [2:115].

Then say:          Salām to you, O my master and the son of my master and O my leader and the son of my leader.                Salām to you, O my master, the Martyr and son of the Martyr, the Slain (One) and the son of the Slain (One). Salām to you and (may) Allāh’s Mercy and Blessings be upon you.                I am performing your Ziyārah, O son of the Messenger of Allāh with my heart, my tongue, and my organs although I have not come to your Ziyārah physically where I can see your dome.

Salām to you, O heir of Ādam, the Chosen Slave of Allāh;     And O heir of Nūḥ, the Prophet of Allāh;     And O heir of Ibrāhīm, the Friend of Allāh;     And O heir of Mūsā, the One Addressed by Allāh;     And O heir of ‘Isā, the Spirit of Allāh;       And O heir of Muḥammad, the Love, the Prophet, and the Messenger of Allāh;        And O heir of ‘Ali, the Commander of the Believers, the Successor of the Messenger of Allāh and his Caliph;       And O heir of Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, the Successor of the Commander of the Believers.
May Allāh’s curse be upon those who killed you and may He renew their torment in this hour and in every hour.

O my master! I seek nearness to Allāh, the Great and Almighty, and to your grandfather, the Messenger of Allāh, and to your father, the Commander of the Believers, and to your brother, Ḥasan, and to you, O my leader, through performing your Ziyārah with my heart, my tongue, and all of my organs. Salām to you and (may) Allāh’s Mercy and Blessings be upon you.

O my master! Intercede on my behalf so that this Ziyārah is accepted from me.             I seek nearness to Allāh and to all of you by dissociating myself from your enemies and by cursing them.      May Allāh’s blessings, His Pleasure, and His Mercy be upon you.
Then move a short distance to the left and turn your face toward the grave of ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (a.s.), who is (buried) next to the feet of his father, and say Salām to him in the same way.

Thereafter, ask Allāh for that which you want with regards to the matters of your religion and your life and then establish four Rak’ah of prayers. Verily the prayers of the Ziyārah can be established in either eight, six, four, or two Rak’ah, and the best is eight Rak’ah.

After the prayers face the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Ḥusain (a.s.)) and say:           I bid farewell to you, O my master and the son of my master and O my leader and the son of my leader.          And I bid farewell to you, O my master and the son of my master, O ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain.       And I bid farewell to you, O my masters, O crowd of Martyrs.
May Allāh’s Salām, His Mercy, His Pleasure, and His Blessings be upon you.
